scope.ddl_keys_and_columns: derived only; not copied into this registry
scope.coverage: selected product tables from registered separated DDL; excludes SQLite internals and runtime-created virtual/shadow tables
scope.python_binding_evidence: AST definition presence plus curated input/projection classification; not serialization or semantic proof
scope.external_reference_scope: catalogue-registered optional external references only; other cross-domain semantics remain unformalized

core.responsibility: Git identity, attributed immutable claims, allowed retained representations and receiver evidence.

context.responsibility: Service/source registrations, generalized resources, attributed relations/text and Context coverage evidence.

access.responsibility: Local connection configuration, locator bindings, scope controls and local approvals.

operational.responsibility: Request orchestration and required durable budgets/accounting/checkpoints; reconstructibility is scoped, not domain-wide.

search.responsibility: Rebuildable search projections, separate from authoritative Core/Context facts.

filesystem.responsibility: Independent historical filesystem metadata/digests and honest scan outcomes, with raw path identity.

worktrees.responsibility: Independent Git topology/worktree observations and explicitly optional qualified links.

Receiver-derived relation evidence qualified by the physical copy used.

Core format/instance metadata; row role says nothing about mutability or recovery policy.
Service-instance UUID registration, distinct from a local connection or access scope.
Source-registration identity and registration payload, independent of source inventory evidence.
Service-scoped typed resource identity; ResourceKey is a value, not this persistent row.
Attributed field candidate with nested resource/clock values and adapter-derived columns.

Scoped resource relation with atomic member representation.

Immutable disposition of an exact mapping claim; not a mutable canonical repository shortcut.

Attributed scoped source inventory evidence, including honest terminal and member coordinates.
Collection scope/registration for a resource; one CollectionObservation input is not a stand-alone row mirror.
One attributed terminal collection observation, independent of collection registration.
Resource-associated nominal Git object coordinate; cross-domain meaning is not a cross-file physical FK.
Context-owned typed coverage coordinate, separate from Core coverage.
One Context coverage claim; shared helper values are not a dedicated row class.
Evidence connecting exact collection terminal and coverage coordinates.
Evidence connecting exact source inventory and coverage coordinates.
Context instance/format metadata; independent of the Core store identity.
Local execution/approval boundary identified by scope UUID.
Append registration occurrence keyed by scope, registration time and raw locator URI.
Mutable enabled control for an exact registration occurrence; not part of the immutable registration payload.
Scope-specific execution configuration; adapter column names need not match Python attribute names.
Named local connection configuration within an Access scope.
Local locator/repository binding, not Core repository identity.
Purpose-specific connection assignment to a local locator.
Local preferred locator/connection for a repository, scope and purpose.
Local approval bound to a reviewed plan; existence does not grant perpetual approval after configuration changes.
Access instance metadata; not a seventh field on an AccessScope.
Explicit durable cumulative work request; retries and continuations do not reset request scope.
Finite request/work-kind budget and cached accounting; actual accounting remains independently checked.
One execution attempt under an explicit request.
Durable reservation/actual-work coordinates; failed or replayed work is not free.
Scoped durable cursor/checkpoint, including canonical Exchange package bindings where used.
Request-scoped retry schedule/reason; no automatic resume after loss of required Operational state.
Locator for reusable metadata/verified-notes cache; reuse never substitutes for required authoritative evidence.
Operational instance identity; required request/recovery state is not classified wholesale as disposable.
Derivative projection generation tied to its exact authority snapshot, not canonical product data.
Searchable derivative document for a qualified projection generation.
Search store metadata; ordinary authoritative reads need not create a Search DB.
Filesystem catalogue namespace/configuration metadata; not a scanned-file entity.
Namespace-qualified scan occurrence with a root_path value; no separate roots table is implied.

Observed termination/partial-result facts for an exact scan; no synthetic completeness.
Independent worktree catalogue identity; does not turn Local composition into a store.
One worktree/topology observation with its own execution scope.
Root-path worktree observation keyed with its enclosing observation UUID.

nonpersistent_types.note: Conceptual shared claim/evidence vocabulary; concrete rows remain separately mapped.
Nominal algorithm/OID value used in many keys; no standalone OID table is required.
Shared attributed-source value; its definition is Contracts-owned, not a claim that Core owns the source module.
Member value embedded in atomic group membership, not one persistent row per Python object.
Validated native object/body input; permitted retention and nominal identity are different row responsibilities.
Read projection over claims/evidence; not a class requiring its own table.
Shared Contracts claim value is reused across Core and Context; distinct qualified persistent classes own their rows.
Composite resource coordinate reused by Context inputs and rows.
Clock value embedded in attributed field/relation coordinates.
Admission aggregate spanning identity and field candidates, not a dedicated resources row mirror.
Input spanning collection scope and terminal evidence; adapters must preserve both responsibilities.
Scoped evidence and positive repository associations can be produced from this aggregate.
Nested scope/locator/configuration/purpose coordinate; not another assignment table.
Root is currently a raw path value in a scan, with no independent persistent Root class or Python Root class claimed.
API result combines scan identity, counts and outcome; it is not the scans table row type.
Read payload includes a computed absolute path using scan context; it is not a raw entries row mirror.
Discovery result supplies enclosing observation context to its worktree payloads.
Scoped payload omits observation_uuid, supplied by its DiscoveryResult/adapter context; cannot stand alone as the complete persistent key.
Query response, including authority fallback, is not the derivative document row class.

gaps.detail: Normal Catalog3 remains mixed Core/Context/Access. Its git_objects surrogate PK differs from separated (object_format, object_oid); normal ref_observations uses (snapshot_id, raw_ref_name), separated uses origin UUIDv4 and observation UUIDv7. Repository UUID identity already exists in both. Equal table names never imply equal row identities. No normal/runtime schema is changed by this model.

A logical persistent class is a design assignment, not a claim that a Python class of that name already exists. Null python means no dedicated row type recorded; SQL/adapters may already implement the complete capability. Observed row inputs may be nested or expand into derived columns. Complete key/field serialization needs later adapter-specific verification.

Filesystem Root is currently root_path within Scan; ScanResult and FileEntry are result/projection types. Do not invent a roots table to match an aggregate or value type. Decide whether independent Root identity is necessary only with its domain semantics.

WorktreeEntry receives observation identity from its enclosing DiscoveryResult/context. A future dedicated Worktree row binding must explicitly include observation_uuid plus root_path; the current scoped DTO is not itself evidence of broken storage.

Context coverage scopes/claims/proofs are real selected tables even if absent from a website concept group. The web branch semantic-model (seven groups of responsibility domains) and older five-store model are derived explanations with different granularities, not canonical table/class maps; their update is independent and deferred.

Only existing catalogue-registered optional external references and DDL physical FKs are checked/rendered. Context/Core references, paired identity rules, operation preconditions, CHECK/trigger semantics, dynamic virtual tables and retained-instance validity are not fully formalized. Coverage success is not complete operation or semantic conformance.

roadmap.detail: Build on existing independent implementations for Core lifecycle including required recovery, Context reads, paired reads/recovery and Access. Assess remaining separated-format adapter/admission/backup/activation gaps against the module operation contract; do not claim these existing capabilities absent. Preserve Core INSERT-only/typed keys, ADR 0038 stop/preserve/typed salvage/fresh verified restore and paired validation. Carry ADR 0039 independent Filesystem/Worktrees raw paths, partial scans, optional qualified references, EFU and DB-free Local composition; those are outside OP-01..12. Fresh DB start needs no legacy conversion; never mutate/delete retained source DBs.

Assess and complete separated-format Operational request orchestration, Git acquisition with optional Access, Exchange and Search integration using existing APIs. Preserve actual cumulative work, durable reservations/checkpoints, package binding and honest loss behavior. Rebuild derivative Search without enlarging authority. Required recovery correctness remains part of foundations, not an optional late add-on.

Only after behavior/adapter tests and recovery prerequisites pass, switch ordinary initialization/CLI composition to fresh separated catalogs. Keep operation-scoped optional initialization: no command must initialize or open all seven DBs simply because the design has seven responsibility roles. This phase is not implemented here.

Remove normal-format factories/adapters and obsolete normal-only tests only after recording each affected test node and its concrete separated-format replacement for the same behavior, including corrupt-source stop, backup/restore, Exchange and accounting failures. Retire tests by obligation, not by coverage counts. No backward-compatibility adapter or old-data migration is required; no authorization to delete user DBs or historical evidence is created.
